metadata.hardware_requirements: Server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650. Quote: "computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)"

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Empirical traffic and video data from a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China, used to calibrate simulation parameters and evaluate the ramp metering method.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Data availability statement explicitly indicates that the data used are available upon request from the corresponding author, with no direct public URL provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: Set up the microscopic traffic simulation using real-world traffic data from the Qingdao-Huangdao freeway tunnel, specifying speed limits and traffic volumes.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, simulator named, core simulation parameters like speed limits and timespan stated explicitly.

nodes_process.source_quote: Three consecutive frames of the traffic video in the controlled area are needed as the observation input
nodes_process.description: Extract vehicle locations to build position matrices, zooming and down-sampling three consecutive video frames to construct the state representation.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, down-sampling tools missing but generic, matrix dimension and frame count stated clearly.

nodes_process.source_quote: the Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer
nodes_process.description: Construct a multi-task deep Q-network using three CNN layers and a fully connected layer to simultaneously predict Q-values, mean speed, and queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, network architecture fully detailed in Figure 7 with exact filter sizes, strides, units, and activation functions.

nodes_process.source_quote: The gradient-based algorithm Adam [28] is used to update wi to minimize the loss function.
nodes_process.description: Train the Deep Q-Network using Experience Replay, Target Network, epsilon-greedy exploration, and the Adam optimizer.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, optimization algorithm and all major hyperparameters are explicitly detailed in Table 1.

nodes_process.source_quote: The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle
nodes_process.description: Configure the PI-ALINEA ramp metering method using downstream occupancies and fixed regulator parameters for baseline comparison.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, the formula and fine-tuned control parameters for PI-ALINEA are completely stated in the text.

nodes_process.source_quote: each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments. The simulations for the training phase and each experiment are initialized with different random seeds.
nodes_process.description: Evaluate the no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL strategies across 20 simulation runs initialized with random seeds, collecting metrics like travel time, speed, and queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, experiment setup is fully described; exact random seeds are missing but the experimental design is clear.

nodes_process.source_quote: The information in the subarea is removed from original data to generate perturbed data for each subarea.
nodes_process.description: Divide the control area into 8 subareas and mask out the visual information in each subarea one by one to evaluate its impact on mean travel time across 20 simulations.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, methodology for masking input data is clear, though specific pixel bounds of the 8 subareas are only visually estimated in Figure 15.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves showing episode reward and mean travel time over 1 million training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear method (SUMO simulation, DRL) but relies on closed empirical base data available only on request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Vehicle travel times in the mainline over time for No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear methodology and aggregation, but tied to a closed empirical dataset.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Mean vehicle travel times (in seconds) and percentage changes for No controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL across 20 simulation runs.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Metrics clearly defined, but raw traffic dataset and random seed details are omitted or closed.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Contour plots of temporal-spatial distribution of speed on the mainline under no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Simulation outputs are well visualized, but underlying traffic demand inputs are not open.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Queue length progression at the on-ramp over time for the three evaluated control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Direct output metric of the SUMO simulation. Bound by closed empirical inputs.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios (i.e., the proportion of the red phase in the simulation time)
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plot correlating queue length and red ratio percentage for PI-ALINEA and Deep RL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clearly plots intermediate simulation metrics; constrained by closed input data.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Time series comparing on-ramp queue length against downstream occupancy for PI-ALINEA and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Coherent comparison derived directly from simulation run logs. Input data closed.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots summarizing downstream traffic volume grouped by 5-minute intervals for the three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear visual aggregation of simulated downstream flows. Cannot be fully reproduced without original traffic profiles.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed
nodes_sink.description: Box plots indicating travel time variations when video data from different perturbed subareas are removed.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Relies on closed data and partially described perturbation mechanisms (exact generation of subarea removal states is somewhat abstract).
